title: The Liquidity Layer is an Agent-scoped name for that Agent's deployment of the shared Allocation System Primitive
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.1 describes the Allocation System Primitive Hub Document as organising "all base information relevant to **Obex's usage of the Obex Liquidity Layer**" — a substitution worth noticing, because every other Hub Document in the Artifact names the Primitive itself at this point.

The naming reveals a two-level model. The **Allocation System Primitive** is the shared specification held at A.2.2.10 and implemented identically by every Agent. The **Liquidity Layer** is the concrete, Agent-owned deployment of it: Obex has an Obex Liquidity Layer, and the same construction appears elsewhere as the Keel Liquidity Layer.

This matters for how the documents should be read. Instance-level provisions elsewhere refer to processes of "the … Liquidity Layer" rather than of the Primitive, meaning they bind that Agent's deployment specifically and cannot be assumed to apply across Agents. Two Agents implementing the same Primitive can run materially different Liquidity Layers.

It also gives each Agent a stable name for a capability that spans many Instances. An Instance is one asset into one venue; the Liquidity Layer is the whole allocation apparatus those Instances belong to, and it is the level at which general operational processes are written — which is precisely why Instance Configuration Documents need a slot for deviating from them.
description: Obex's Allocation System Primitive Hub organises "Obex's usage of the Obex Liquidity Layer", mirroring the Keel Liquidity Layer — one Primitive specification, per-Agent branded instantiations.
